title: LP1: the 464-word table and column balance
question: Does the stated ordered 464-word object have unusually low variance among 16 column means under unrestricted permutations of its fixed word lengths?
summary: All 464 supplied lengths reproduce from archived runes. Sixteen column means have R=0.25150357; 54 of 49,999 unrestricted shuffles are at least as flat (corrected p=0.0011). This selected arrangement does not establish authorial intent.

scope.representation: Archived ciphertext runes, headings and interrupting F retained. Join slash and newline wraps and consecutive pages within a section. Rune runs with internal apostrophes form one word; apostrophes count zero runes. Other non-runes delimit words. Never merge sections.
scope.procedure: Concatenate Warning, Welcome, first koan and second koan in that order; count native runes per word. Compare all 464 values with the supplied vector. Fill 29 rows of 16 columns across rows without resetting at sections. Measure population variance of the 16 column means and divide by its exact finite-population shuffle expectation. Each trial freshly copies and uniformly shuffles the fixed 464 lengths; compare integer scores proportional to variance.
scope.parameters: 16 columns; 29 words per column; 49,999 shuffles; Python random.Random seed 330146; lower tail including ties; (tail_count+1)/50000; threshold 0.05. Arrangement and approximate ratio were known before the frozen simulation plan.
scope.exclusions: Other widths, section orders, constrained shuffles, prose corpus comparisons, sentence removal, section cancellation, grille extraction, carrier matching, original-search multiplicity, authorial intent and decryption.

finding: All 464 word lengths reproduce from the archived runes. The sixteen column averages are unusually even under the stated shuffle model: their variance is 25.15% of its expectation. Only 54 of 49,999 shuffles were at least as even (corrected lower-tail p=0.0011). A full rerun and independent checks agree.
limitations: This is an explored, selected arrangement. The p-value does not adjust for the original search and is not the probability of coincidence or intent. Unrestricted shuffling destroys sentence and section structure; it is not a coherent-prose comparison. Reported corpus and carrier findings remain unverified. Human review pending.
next_steps: Section-preserving shuffles, all 24 section orders and a six-width search are published as lp1-section-balance, lp1-section-order and lp1-width-selection. Sentence-preserving comparisons, corpus conversion, sentence-removal and carrier claims require separately frozen inputs and procedures.

family.title: LP1 word lengths and column balance
family.question: How unusual is the ordered four-section word-length arrangement under explicitly bounded comparisons?

review.reviewer: Codex — full rerun; independent token scanner and rational variance; exhaustive toy null expectations; first 32 null scores independently calculated; complete tail audit; human review pending

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12.10 standard library. Independent check: python experiments/records/lp1-word-length-balance/check.py

research_questions.question: Does the balance remain unusual when each section keeps its own word lengths?
research_questions.note: The table remains unusually balanced in this comparison: only 88 of 49,999 shuffles were at least as even. Keeping each section’s word lengths changes the comparison, but this is still the same previously selected table, not independent confirmation.

research_questions.question: Does the result survive checking every order of the four sections?
research_questions.note: The original order ties for best. When every shuffled sample also tries all 24 orders, 440 of 49,999 are at least as balanced. That accounts for choosing the section order; it does not account for choosing these words or the table width.

research_questions.question: What happens when six table widths are compared?
research_questions.note: The six-width search did not distinguish the manuscript from shuffled controls: 6,035 of 49,999 were at least as balanced after the same search. These controls shuffle across sections. This tests a different choice rule from the fixed 16-column comparison.

research_questions.question: Does the balance remain unusual when sentence structure is preserved?
research_questions.note: This needs reliable sentence breaks and one fixed rule: rearrange words inside each sentence, or move whole sentences without changing their words. Those are different comparisons; neither has a prepared test here.

visuals.caption: Mean rune-word length in each of 16 columns, with 29 words per column. The dashed line is the overall mean. This depicts the observed arrangement, not its null distribution or evidence of deliberate construction.
